faq.q: What exactly is a money detox?
faq.a: A money detox is a temporary, intentional period (usually a month) where you significantly reduce or eliminate non-essential spending to gain clarity on your financial habits and reset your relationship with money.

faq.q: How long should a money detox last?
faq.a: Typically, a money detox lasts for one month. This duration is usually long enough to observe significant changes in spending patterns and break some habits, yet short enough to be sustainable without feeling overly restrictive.

faq.q: Will a money detox negatively affect my credit score?
faq.a: No, a money detox focuses on reducing spending, not on defaulting on payments. As long as you continue to pay your bills and EMIs on time, your credit score will not be negatively impacted. In fact, by freeing up funds, you might even be able to pay down credit card debt faster.

faq.q: Can I still invest during a money detox?
faq.a: Absolutely. A money detox primarily targets discretionary spending. Essential financial commitments like SIPs, insurance premiums, and loan EMIs should continue as usual. The goal is to free up *more* money for investments, not to stop them.

faq.q: What if an emergency expense comes up during my money detox?
faq.a: Emergencies are an exception. A money detox is about controlling discretionary spending, not about sacrificing genuine needs or safety. If an emergency arises, address it as necessary. The detox is a tool for financial health, not a rigid rule to be broken at your peril.

faq.q: How do I maintain good habits after the detox ends?
faq.a: The detox helps you identify triggers and areas of overspending. After the detox, gradually reintroduce some 'wants' but with greater mindfulness. Continue tracking your expenses, stick to a budget, and regularly review your financial goals to sustain the positive changes.
